definition.title: Spectroscopy Lab
learning_objectives: Connect ideal blackbody temperature to continuum shape and Wien peak wavelength.
Distinguish continuous, emission-line, and absorption-line teaching spectra.
Relate radial velocity to first-order wavelength shift using a bounded astronomy-scale Doppler model.
Relate resolving power to the width of illustrative spectral features.
Compare a small set of source-backed atomic fingerprints without treating the synthetic spectrum as abundance inference.

fields.name: mode
fields.meaning: One of continuum, emission, absorption, doppler, or element_match.

fields.name: selected_elements
fields.meaning: Unique subset of H I, He I, Na I, and Ca II. Required for every non-continuum mode.

fields.name: radial_velocity_km_s
fields.sign_convention: Positive is recession/redshift; negative is approach/blueshift.

fields.name: noise_seed
fields.meaning: Explicit deterministic seed used by the SHA-256/Box-Muller v1 display-noise algorithm.

input_schema.invalid_handling: Reject unknown modes/species, duplicate species, missing line species outside continuum mode, booleans/non-finite values, and all out-of-range values. No scientific input is silently clamped.

output_schema: 741 deterministic spectrum samples from 380.0 through 750.0 nm vacuum wavelength
normalized flux in the display interval 0..1
physical Wien peak wavelength from the reviewed CODATA displacement constant
first-order Doppler factor and exact rest/shifted representative line metadata
illustrative Gaussian FWHM for each representative line from R=lambda/delta-lambda
selected element fingerprint explanation and explicit modelling caveats

equations.planck_wavelength_shape: B_lambda proportional to 1 / [lambda^5 * (exp(h*c/(lambda*k*T)) - 1)]; v1 normalizes the returned visible-range curve rather than exposing physical radiance units
equations.resolving_power: R = lambda/delta_lambda; v1 illustrative Gaussian FWHM = lambda_observed/R
equations.noise: SHA-256(seed,index) -> two open-interval uniforms -> Box-Muller standard normal -> sigma-scaled normalized display noise

definition.sampling_policy: Return exactly 741 samples at 0.5 nm spacing from 380.0 through 750.0 nm. Atomic line metadata retains the exact reviewed observed-vacuum centers even when a line center lies between sampled points. Noise is deterministic and applied only after canonical continuum/line synthesis.
definition.default_preset: Illustrative Solar-like absorption teaching spectrum: 5772 K, H I + Na I + Ca II, zero radial velocity, R=500, zero noise.
assumptions: The continuum is an ideal blackbody shape normalized over the visible 380-750 nm output interval.
Selected NIST ASD observed-vacuum line centers are representative teaching fingerprints, not a complete line list.
All representative lines use equal illustrative profile strength; NIST relative intensities are not used as physical amplitudes.
Emission mode uses a zero baseline with equal normalized Gaussian features.
Absorption, Doppler, and element-match modes use a fixed illustrative absorption depth on the normalized blackbody continuum.
Resolving power is represented by a Gaussian teaching profile with FWHM=lambda/R.
Optional noise is deterministic normalized display noise, not an instrument/photon noise model.
limitations: No LTE/non-LTE atmosphere, radiative transfer, abundance, ionization/excitation balance, opacity, or equivalent-width modelling.
No oscillator-strength-weighted or NIST-relative-intensity-weighted line strengths.
No pressure, thermal, rotational, turbulent, Zeeman, Stark, or natural broadening model beyond the illustrative instrumental Gaussian.
No detector throughput, response curve, wavelength calibration, sky/telluric spectrum, extinction/reddening, photon noise, read noise, or flux calibration.
The first-order Doppler law is restricted to +/-300 km/s and is not a relativistic/high-redshift model.
Element-match mode explains selected representative fingerprints; it does not infer unknown composition or chemical abundance.
The returned normalized spectrum is an educational representation and must not be compared quantitatively to observed physical flux without a separate calibrated model.

line_selection_policy.selection: Explicit small pedagogical subset of NIST ASD observed-vacuum features. Repeated ASD fine-structure rows sharing one identical observed wavelength are one observed feature. No handbook-air conversion and no invented centroid are used.
line_selection_policy.intensity_use: NIST relative intensity strings are retained only as provenance context and are not used to synthesize amplitudes.

validation_fixtures.purpose: 5772 K returns a Wien peak near 502 nm from the reviewed CODATA displacement constant.
Continuum mode returns 741 positive deterministic samples with a visible-range maximum of exactly one after normalization.
Emission mode metadata retains exact reviewed NIST rest centers and applies only the reviewed Doppler factor.
Absorption mode lowers the normalized continuum near selected line centers without changing the source-backed line metadata.
Positive velocity redshifts and negative velocity blueshifts according to delta-lambda/lambda=v/c.
Representative-line FWHM is observed wavelength divided by resolving power and narrows monotonically as R rises.
The supported species and exact selected observed-vacuum line list match the reviewed NIST ASD artifact.
Identical seed/sigma/input produce bit-for-bit identical normalized spectrum samples.
Different seeds produce a different deterministic display-noise realization when noise_sigma is nonzero.
Unknown modes/elements, duplicate elements, and non-continuum modes without selected elements fail closed.
Booleans, non-finite values, and temperature/velocity/resolution/noise/seed values outside the reviewed bounds fail closed.
Version/source/constant/line-list/preset/noise-policy drift is rejected by the strict artifact loader.

scientific_validation.method: Validate normalized Planck/Wien behavior, source-backed NIST observed-vacuum line centers, first-order Doppler sign/scale, resolving-power FWHM, deterministic seeded noise, strict domains, and artifact integrity. Do not validate illustrative line amplitudes as physical predictions.
